The Institute at its founding resolved to protect the daylight world from the dangers of the invisible arts - even if that meant upholding the tyranny of Calyptra. Its founders never guessed how challenging that would be. The War in the Sun brought an end to the established order. With so many Hours uncounted or fled - with the horrors of the old spirits and the new weapons ravaging Europe - with the Gleam-touched Ministries rising in the East, and the Glory-crowned Incorporates of the West - it was impossible to maintain the laws of secrecy. The Institute set itself to the protection of the most dangerous knowledge, and the education of its seekers. And the centre of that endeavour remains - of course - Hush House: where the Librarian, as always, keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Rocks are no sharper in the dark.']

The Institute at its founding resolved to undermine Calyptra. Its founders never guessed how successful they could be. The War in the Sun brought an end to the established order. With so many Hours uncounted or fled - with the horrors of the old spirits and the new weapons ravaging Europe - with the Gleam-touched Ministries rising in the East, and the Glory-crowned Incorporates of the West - the laws of secrecy crumbled. The Institute set itself to guarding knowledge and guiding its seekers. And the centre of that endeavour remains - of course - Hush House: where the Librarian, as always, keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Every lighthouse needs a lamp at the top and rocks at the bottom.'']

The Institute could not prevent the coming war, any more than a lighthouse could prevent a storm. And so the storm broke, on Europe and the world. But how many bodies did they save? And how many souls? Through the falls of the Stars and the rise of the Incorporates, through all the plagues of Worm and amber, the Institute built havens, found time and strength for its guests to build bridges. And the oldest, the kindest, the strongest of those havens was Hush House... where the Librarian still keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Silence after lightning; silence before thunder.']

The Institute in silence unearthed the secrets of the Hours that came before. When War came to the Mansus and the Wake, they preserved those secrets for an uncertain future. They learnt of their predecessors: the ones who had been called the Obliviates, and their nameless precursors who had served the same role beneath a redder sun. And so the Institute became another fire-forged link in the wisdom-chain that runs into the dawn. Knowledge endures; books are the memory that does not die; and nowhere is this more true than at Hush House, where the Librarian still keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'The waves leave what the world's lost.']

The Institute never found a clear mission, beyond the preservation of its own privacy and the advancement of its members' interests. But through the War in the World and the War in the Sun, as Europe convulsed and the skies wrung out their cargo of blood and Stars, the Institute remained, persisted, endured, in the shadow of the long traditions of the Obliviates and of the Curia of the Isle; through all that time, the Librarian remained at Hush House and kept their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Hush House endures; the Institute persists']

The Institute set itself to feed the conflicts that feed the world… and the world went up like naphtha beneath an open flame. It was inevitable; the Institute's provocations were one cause among a hundred; and if some of the founders regret their part, still the War in the World and the War in the Sun made for unimaginable opportunities - profits both visible and invisible. In the ruins of the new Europe, the Institute is a hidden power, carving out its own domain between other spheres of influence - the Glory-crowned Incorporates of the West, the Gleam-touched Ministries of the East. Much has changed since its birth at Hush House - but Hush House still stands, under the Institute's protection, and there the Librarian still keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Only twins drown twice.']

The Wars, above and below, ravaged the waking world, the Mansus, and the Sun… and the Institute seized the opportunity. Following the strategy of a capricious, visionary immortal - not without misgivings - they worked with the Crown, with rebellious Forge-long, with the Gleam-touched, to construct surrogate Hours. With so many Hours now uncounted in the war, their timing could not have been better. Their surrogates have brought stability to a shattered Europe. But they have not been exactly loyal to the Institute, and the Institute remains in the background. But the background is where all its members are most comfortable; not least the Librarian, who, silent before the sunset glimmerings of the Brancrug sea, keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Every flame has its fuel; every fuel fears its flame.']

The institute stands for all humanity, but first of all it stands for continuity… and before anything else, this must mean the continuity of the Institute. So while the War in the Sun ravaged the invisible world, and the War in the World ravaged Europe, the Institute husbanded its resources and deployed them judiciously - protecting a site of interest here, a looted collection there. Now that the wars are past, the Institute has staked a claim to a hidden Alpine valley, where it protects those it finds sufficiently interesting, and builds its plans for the future: a brighter, wider world beyond the reach of the Ministries of the Gleam-touched East, the Coronal Incorporates of the West. But the Institute's root and heart remains Hush House, the fortress of knowledge where the Librarian still keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Every cliff a fortress; every hermitage a mountain.']

Through the years of the War in the World and the War in the Sun, the Institute shattered prehuman altars in search of secrets, excavated the corpses of primordial colossi to render them to wisdom. The caution of the old Curia and of the Obliviates had given way to a new ruthlessness. They emerged as one of the hidden powers of the new Europe, treating profitably with the Gleam-touched Ministries and Glory-gifted Incorporates. From the shadows, they helped guide the continent back towards the light... and in the shadows, the lights of Hush House still glow across the water, and the Librarian still keeps their solitary counsel. [You have founded the Lighthouse Institute. Its motto: 'Many pebbles, one Beach.']
